newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wary German shares open lower, RWE bucks trend.
newsitem.headline: Wary German shares open lower, RWE bucks trend.

text.p: German shares started out weaker on Thursday, as tension mounted ahead of the release of key U.S. economic data.

Blue chip stocks opened broadly lower, with chemical shares under particular pressure after interim data from BASF, while utility group RWE AG surged against trend on news it planned to scrap multiple voting rights on a chunk of its shares.
The 30-share DAX index was down 52.03 points at 4,226.45 an hour into bourse trade, having risen from a low of 4,200.23.
September DTB DAX futures were down two at 4,244 points.
Dealers said the market was likely to move in a fairly narrow range ahead of a rash of indicators coming from the United States from 1230 GMT.

The data, including weekly U.S. jobless claims, July consumer prices and industrial production, are expected to throw further light on the U.S. economy -- crucial to the German market which is currently highly vulnerable to swings on the U.S. financial markets.

RWE shares were up 7.60 marks, or 9.5 percent, at 87.60 marks on news of the voting rights move. Holders of shares with multiple voting rights, mainly municipalities, will be invited to swap these for shares with standard voting rights.
The move is viewed as opening up the company to international investors by loosening the hold municipalities have on its equity.
Among the big corporate news of the morning were half-year results from chemical giant BASF AG, which put pressure on its shares and those of other chemical groups.
BASF said net income in the first half of the year was up 3.4 percent at 1.417 billion marks, while sales were up 14.5 percent at 27.797 billion marks, at the lower end of analysts' expectations.
BASF was down 3.40 marks at 68.80 marks, Hoechst fell 4.30 marks to 76.70 marks and Bayer dropped 2.30 marks to 73.50 marks.
